content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To go to the library downtown, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Walk through the library main entrance (30 seconds)
Step 2. Use the self-checkout kiosk (2 minutes)
Step 3. Put on a warm coat (1 minute)
Step 4. Check the library operating hours online (2 minutes)
Step 5. Locate your physical library card (5 minutes)
Step 6. Check the weather forecast (1 minute)
Step 7. Place the library card in your wallet (30 seconds)
Step 8. Check your bag for any overdue books (3 minutes)
Step 9. Walk from the bus stop to the library building (8 minutes)
Step 10. Research which floor the history books are on (4 minutes)
Step 11. Browse the new arrivals shelf (15 minutes)
Step 12. Make a list of specific book titles (10 minutes)
Step 13. Walk from the sidewalk to the library stairs (1 minute)
Step 14. Decide which branch to visit (2 minutes)
Step 15. Walk out the front door of your house (1 minute)
Step 16. Charge your phone for the trip (20 minutes)
Step 17. Cross the street toward the library (2 minutes)
Step 18. Put on your shoes (2 minutes)
Step 19. Check that you have your house keys (30 seconds)
Step 20. Ask the librarian for a recommendation (5 minutes)
Step 21. Find a quiet desk to sit at (2 minutes)
Step 22. Look up the call numbers for your books (5 minutes)
Step 23. Locate the specific bookshelf in the stacks (5 minutes)
Step 24. Look up the bus schedule (5 minutes)
Step 25. Put your laptop in your backpack (1 minute)
Step 26. Check if you have enough money for the bus fare (2 minutes)
Step 27. Select a book from the shelf (1 minute)
Step 28. Lock the front door (30 seconds)
Step 29. Walk to the neighborhood bus stop (10 minutes)
Step 30. Check the library's special events calendar (3 minutes)
Step 31. Board the downtown bus (15 minutes)
Step 32. Pay the bus driver (30 seconds)
Step 33. Exit the bus at the downtown station (1 minute)
Step 34. Tell your roommate where you are going (1 minute)
Step 35. Set your phone to silent mode (10 seconds)
Step 36. Walk toward the library information desk (2 minutes)
Step 37. Walk down the library hallway (2 minutes)
Step 38. Wave hello to the security guard (10 seconds)
Step 39. Ride the bus for the duration of the route (25 minutes)
Step 40. Find your tote bag for carrying books (2 minutes)
Step 41. Decide which genre you want to read (5 minutes)
Step 42. Double check that the windows are closed (3 minutes)
Step 43. Walk through the library courtyard (3 minutes)
Step 44. Walk up the library's concrete steps (1 minute)
Step 45. Put a bookmark in your pocket (10 seconds)
Step 46. Turn off the lights in the house (30 seconds)
Step 47. Clean your glasses (1 minute)
Step 48. Check that you have your umbrella (1 minute)
Step 49. Gather your belongings (4 minutes)
Step 50. Unplug your laptop charger (15 seconds)
